papers.title: iPscDB: a comprehensive platform for plant single-cell transcriptomic data integration and analysis.
papers.summary: iPscDB integrates 4.69 million plant cells and 288,139 curated markers from 946 experiments across 38 species, reprocessed through one uniform pipeline with benchmarked annotation. It adds marker confidence grading, an online analysis pipeline accepting FASTQ or Cell Ranger inputs, and cross-species, pictograph, and trajectory modules, making plant single-cell analysis accessible without programming expertise.

papers.title: Epigenetic training licenses naïve CD8(+) T cell metabolic fitness and function.
papers.summary: Naive CD8+ T cells are epigenetically pre-trained for future activation: histone variant H2A.z, deposited at oxidative phosphorylation gene promoters under tonic IL-7 signaling via transcription factor Gabpalpha, primes rapid transcription. Aging reduces this via declining IL-7; supplementation or enforced H2A.z rescues activation and enhances CAR-T stemness and antitumor efficacy.

papers.title: A compact, wireless fluorimeter system for continuous, real-time monitoring of tissue perfusion via in vivo fluorescence signals.
papers.summary: Researchers built a compact, wireless, wearable fluorimeter for continuous real-time fluorescence measurements anywhere on the body, streaming to smart devices. Compatible with clinically used injectable fluorophores (indocyanine green, fluorescein, methylene blue), it produced physiologically meaningful readouts in ischemic rodents, healthy pigs, and amputation/replantation models, validated against ex situ blood analysis.

papers.title: Functional diversity of natural human IFNB1 variants in innate immunity.
papers.summary: The authors functionally tested 70 rare naturally occurring human IFNB1 variants. A quarter were less active than reference IFN-beta, often from ER retention or impaired IFNAR1/IFNAR2 binding, while three variants showed enhanced receptor engagement, signaling, and antiviral potency. The survey frames IFNB1 variation for disease association and next-generation interferon therapeutics.

papers.title: An automated high-resolution screening platform identifies regulators of anchor cell invasion in C. elegans.
papers.summary: A user-friendly automated microfluidic imaging platform for C. elegans, combined with a neural-network scorer exceeding 92% accuracy, imaged over 40,000 animals at subcellular resolution in an RNAi screen of 193 genes regulating anchor cell invasion, a model of basement membrane breaching. It recovered 41 known invasion genes and found 51 new regulators.

papers.title: Systems biology framework for the rational design of operational conditions for in vitro/in vivo translation of tissue models.
papers.summary: Liv2Trans is a machine-learning framework mapping microphysiological liver models (MPS) onto in vivo data to nominate culture conditions improving human translatability, using MASLD as a case study. It identified TGF-beta as a key cue and showed interferon-mediated JAK-STAT perturbations improve MPS predictive performance, offering a generalizable approach for disease modeling.

papers.title: GTPase cycle and ER membrane regulate cargo handover during cotranslational protein targeting.
papers.summary: Using pre-steady-state and single-molecule fluorescence, this study resolves how SRP hands nascent cargo to the ER translocon. The SR receptor releases the signal sequence from SRP yet tethers SRP to the ribosome; GTP hydrolysis abolishes this tethering, and the ER membrane promotes a prehandover conformation where delayed GTP hydrolysis optimizes targeting-to-translocation transition.

papers.title: Rejuvenating endogenous antitumor immunity via a chimeric receptor-engineered oncolytic virus targeting tumor-associated macrophages.
papers.summary: A modular oncolytic herpesvirus engineered with a PD-L1-specific chimeric receptor in its envelope (CAR-oHSV) targets both tumor cells and PD-L1+ tumor-associated macrophages. It reprograms TAMs via STING into a CXCL9+ cross-presenting phenotype, sparking endogenous antitumor T cells, and synergizes with adoptive T cell and checkpoint therapies in resistant models.

papers.title: Cobalt-mediated suppression of IFN-γ-JAK-STAT1 signaling reprograms IDO1-driven immunosuppression for metalloimmunotherapy.
papers.summary: Cobalt ions suppress IFN-gamma-induced IDO1 by destabilizing IFNGR1 and blocking JAK-STAT1 signaling, restoring kynurenine/tryptophan balance and relieving immunosuppression of CD8+ T cells. Encapsulated in a hyaluronic-acid nanoparticle (CoNaha) for tumor-targeted delivery, cobalt improved checkpoint blockade efficacy across multiple mouse tumor models including pancreatic KPC.

papers.title: Ubiquitin receptor-mediated, ubiquitin-independent targeted protein degradation via 26S proteasomes.
papers.summary: ProteaTAC is a targeted protein degradation platform that recruits substrates directly to 26S proteasomes via a ubiquitin-receptor plus intracellular antibody chimera, bypassing ubiquitination. It degraded c-Fos, BRD4, TDP43, tau, and others modularly and specifically, and showed in vivo antitumor efficacy through both viral and nonviral delivery in c-Fos-dependent tumors.

papers.title: Targeting glial PD-1/PD-L1 restores microglial homeostasis and reduces neuronal hyperactivity in an Alzheimer's disease model.
papers.summary: In 5xFAD Alzheimer's mice, intracortical anti-PD-L1 blockade restored microglial homeostasis—improved process convergence and P2RY12 expression—and reduced aberrant neuronal hyperactivity. Astrocyte-specific PD-L1 knockdown mimicked this, indicating astrocytic PD-L1 regulates microglia-neuron interactions. The glial PD-1/PD-L1 axis thus acts as a brain-intrinsic immune checkpoint relevant to AD.

papers.title: A high-density CRISPR activation platform for mapping cancer dependencies and resistance pathways ex vivo and in vivo.
papers.summary: Partita is a next-generation mouse whole-genome CRISPR activation platform with 10 sgRNAs per transcription start site across five gene-class sublibraries. Demonstrated screens—including genome-wide ex vivo screens for resistance to venetoclax, nutlin-3a, and etoposide, and an in vivo MYC-lymphoma screen—revealed expected and unexpected regulators with high validation rates.

papers.title: Super-enhancer-driven SGK1 activates polyamine metabolism to promote autoimmune uveitis.
papers.summary: Combining CUT&Tag with single-cell RNA-seq in Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada uveitis, super-enhancer-driven SGK1 was upregulated in CD4+ T cells and activates MEK-ERK-ODC1 polyamine metabolism, skewing Th17/Treg balance. SGK1 inhibition alleviated mouse uveitis, and the natural compound herbacetin emerged as an SGK1 inhibitor restoring immune balance, nominating SGK1 for therapy.

papers.title: Secreted ORF8 reprograms macrophages to enhance SARS-CoV-2 infection of lung epithelial cells.
papers.summary: SARS-CoV-2 secreted ORF8 increases macrophage permissiveness to infection, triggering pyroptosis and amplifying viral replication in alveolar type II cells, overriding ORF8's previously reported direct infection inhibition. IL-17RA blockade counteracted ORF8 in vivo, lowering viral burden, inflammation, and fibrosis—defining a paracrine proviral circuit accelerating COVID-19 lung pathology.

papers.title: Microbiota-derived indole limits Campylobacter jejuni colonization by inhibiting respiration and metabolism.
papers.summary: DSS-induced colitis in conventional mice broke colonization resistance to Campylobacter jejuni within three days, depleting indole-producing microbiota. Indole physiologically inhibited C. jejuni by downregulating respiration and energy pathways (napA, ccoN, lctP, ackA/pta), and indole or probiotic E. coli Nissle 1917 reduced colonization, showing microbiota-derived metabolites suppress the pathogen.

papers.title: A built-in brake for plant immunity: Resistance (R) protein-mediated immunity is fine-tuned by R gene analogs.
papers.summary: Durable potato R8 resistance to late blight is fine-tuned by linked R8 gene analogs (RGAs) lacking resistance function: they perturb AVR8 recognition by R8 and interfere with helper NLR NRC2 oligomerization and membrane association. Overexpression compromises R8 immunity, suggesting endogenous negative regulation reduces pathogen selection pressure, prolonging resistance durability.

papers.title: Diversity of electron-bifurcating CO(2)-fixing supercomplexes in methanogens.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM-style structural analysis reports a C2-symmetric (Mvh-Hdr)2-Fmd4 supercomplex from Methanothermobacter marburgensis, architecturally distinct from the D3-symmetric form of class II methanogens. Two MVHB polyferredoxins connect HDR and FMD active sites with branching electron paths; ancestry modeling suggests C2 symmetry was ancestral, with D3 acquired by horizontal gene transfer for substrate-poor niches.

papers.title: PAX3-SIX2 muscle stem cell heterogeneity drives muscle-specific repair dynamics diversification.
papers.summary: Lineage tracing shows the embryonic myogenic regulator PAX3 marks a muscle-specific subset of adult PAX7+ stem cells whose proportion varies by muscle. PAX3+ cells, which express SIX2 under PAX3 control, proliferate and differentiate faster after injury; SIX2 ectopic expression rescues proliferation. PAX3-SIX2 heterogeneity thus diversifies regeneration rates across muscles.

papers.title: A suite of fluorescent timers for visualizing protein spatiotemporal dynamics in plants.
papers.summary: This resource systematically evaluates fluorescent timer configurations in Arabidopsis, identifying tandem fluorescent timers matching plant maturation kinetics. Validated across organelles and applications—autoimmunity, abiotic-stress transport, and cell-fate polar trafficking—the work also introduces bipartite timers for cases where timer size hinders protein mobility, guiding spatiotemporal protein dynamics studies in plants.

papers.title: Endothelial C/EBPβ/AEP pathway drives vascular deterioration and systemic aging.
papers.summary: Aging endothelial cells activate C/EBPbeta-asparagine endopeptidase (AEP) signaling; endothelial overexpression of either accelerates vascular aging and shortens mouse lifespan. AEP cleaves NAMPT, depleting NAD+ and driving senescence. AEP ablation, an AEP-resistant NAMPT mutant, an AEP inhibitor, or nicotinamide mononucleotide supplementation ameliorated decline, nominating C/EBPbeta-AEP as an aging target.

papers.title: Serpin-driven green camouflage and NIR fluorescence in frogs.
papers.summary: Tree frogs evolved biliverdin-binding serpins (BBSs) that stabilize biliverdin with receptor-like affinity, tuning its spectrum for leaf-like green camouflage; some lineages show near-infrared fluorescence. A glassfrog BBS is naturally proteolytically cleaved yet keeps binding, decoupling serpin cleavage from ligand retention, and photoacoustic tomography mapped body-wide BBS distribution—insights for NIR probe design.

papers.title: Uncovering structural variation in conifer gigagenomes: evolutionary insights and technical challenges.
papers.summary: Long-read plus short-read sequencing across three hybridizing pine species identified 5.7 million structural variants—mostly intergenic and transposable-element-associated—with hundreds-fold higher loss-of-function rates than SNPs. Graph pangenome SV genotyping showed only modest recall and limited overlap with SNP selection scans, demonstrating SVs capture complementary adaptive variation in conifer gigagenomes.

papers.title: Mycn facilitates hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell generation from endothelial cells by inhibiting adhesion signaling.
papers.summary: Endothelial MYCN, not MYC, is required for hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell generation during the endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition. Mycn-deficient hemogenic endothelium aberrantly maintains adhesion signaling; single-cell profiling and mosaic analysis support this, and focal adhesion kinase inhibition rescues HSPC production, positioning adhesion suppression as MYCN's key role.

papers.title: Transcriptomics reveals metabolic division of labor and reproduction-metabolism decoupling in Saccharomyces cerevisiae biofilms.
papers.summary: Spatiotemporal transcriptomics of industrial yeast biofilms reveals a reproduction-metabolism decoupling: outer cells form a stress-tolerant metabolic shield maximizing glycolysis via retrograde signaling, while inner cells proliferate in a protected nursery. This self-organizing division of labor explains biofilm resilience and offers a blueprint for spatially programmed microbial factories.

papers.title: MYZAP promotes angiogenesis by targeting RND1 after myocardial infarction.
papers.summary: MYZAP expression drops after myocardial infarction; endothelial-specific overexpression improved cardiac function and angiogenesis. Mechanistically, MYZAP binds RND1 directly, sequestering it from RND1 overexpression's anti-angiogenic effect, with TRIM21 identified as RND1's E3 ligase, activating VEGF/PI3K/AKT signaling that restores endothelial proliferation, migration, and tube formation under hypoxia.

papers.title: Integrative proteomics defines FANCA as a multifunctional hub linking DNA repair to translation.
papers.summary: An integrative interactomics strategy (co-immunoprecipitation, proximity labeling, network integration) mapped FANCA interaction landscapes beyond the Fanconi core and DNA repair, revealing engagement with chromatin remodeling, RNA metabolism, and ribosome biogenesis. Quantitative proteomics showed altered ribosome protein stoichiometry, linking FANCA to translation and explaining Fanconi anemia's pleiotropy.

papers.title: CHAC1-linked NRF2 protein expression participates in pancreatic islet protection by dextrorphan.
papers.summary: The NMDA antagonist dextrorphan protects pancreatic islets by upregulating NRF2 target genes, but also induces pro-apoptotic CHAC1. Silencing CHAC1 enhanced protection, while NRF2 knockdown or inhibition diminished it; NRF2 activation didn't add benefit. Dextrorphan's efficacy thus requires NRF2 but is capped by concomitant CHAC1 upregulation in islet cytoprotection.

papers.title: Epitope-driven polyfunctional divergence of SARS-CoV-2 RBD antibodies.
papers.summary: Profiling memory B cell antibodies from ancestral SARS-CoV-2 infection shows class 1/3 neutralizing RBD antibodies lose Omicron binding yet retain Fc effector functions (ADCC, phagocytosis, complement) and allosterically enhance fusion-peptide antibody binding. Broadly reactive non-neutralizers targeting conserved epitopes cross-react but lack effector functions, applying minimal immune pressure.

papers.title: Oxytocin receptor signaling contributes to the mitochondrial integrity and maintain gastric mucosal homeostasis in male mice.
papers.summary: In mice, oxytocin receptor (OXTR) signaling in gastric parietal cells maintains mucosal homeostasis: OXTR/OXT deficiency caused mucosal hyperplasia, and high-fat diet induced hyperplasia, parietal cell atrophy, mitochondrial damage, and impaired glucose uptake—reversed by oxytocin in wild-type but not OXTR-null mice, implicating OXTR in mitochondrial integrity of the stomach.

papers.title: Behavioral states affect eye position tuning in the parietal cortex of macaques.
papers.summary: Comparing task-constrained fixation to spontaneous gaze fixations in darkness, macaque V6A neurons showed similar firing rates but stronger eye-position spatial tuning during spontaneous fixation, with more variable responses under constraint. Spatial representations in parietal cortex thus flexibly engage across behavioral states beyond goal-directed visuomotor processing.

papers.title: CTLA-4 haploinsufficiency leads to late-onset autoimmune pathology in mice.
papers.summary: A heterozygous patient-derived Y139C Ctla-4 mouse model showed young animals develop lymphoproliferation and T cell activation with impaired trans-endocytosis yet no autoimmunity; with aging, spontaneous autoimmune manifestations emerged despite compensatory CTLA-4-independent Treg suppression. The study confirms CTLA-4 haploinsufficiency pathogenicity and reveals age-dependent penetrance.

papers.title: Piezoelectric amino acids and peptides: Mechanisms, molecular engineering, and biomedical applications.
papers.summary: This review covers piezoelectric amino acids and peptides: their mechanisms, classification, molecular modification, and external-field-assisted fabrication, alongside biomedical applications in biosensing, tissue regeneration, antimicrobial therapy, and cancer treatment. Their biocompatibility, biodegradability, and bioelectric-like signals position them for biodegradable bioelectronics, with challenges and clinical translation directions outlined.

papers.title: Green synthesis of pyridine-benzofuran hybrids with anti-inflammatory activity alongside in silico study.
papers.summary: Pyridine-benzofuran hybrids were green-synthesized via multicomponent reaction and tested in rat carrageenan paw edema. Compounds 7a and 7e showed dose-dependent edema inhibition (61.2% and 60.3% at 200 mg/kg) versus indomethacin; docking against COX-2 and 100-ns dynamics on 7a confirmed stable binding, establishing 7a as an anti-inflammatory lead candidate.

papers.title: A novel mitochondrial microprotein reprograms cellular bioenergetics and protects against hepatic steatosis.
papers.summary: Organelle-enriched proteomics with a custom sORF database uncovered MNP33, a 28-amino-acid mitochondrial microprotein. In mice it reduces weight gain, improves glucose homeostasis, and cuts hepatic triacylglycerol. Localizing to the inner mitochondrial membrane, MNP33 binds ANT2 and remodels bioenergetics—raising proton leak and respiration—providing a direct route to lipid dissipation in MASLD.

papers.title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis is associated with aldosterone overproduction in idiopathic hyperaldosteronism.
papers.summary: Integrating Mendelian randomization, metagenomics of 30 idiopathic hyperaldosteronism patients and 30 controls, and metabolomics, the study links gut dysbiosis—lower diversity and depleted protective taxa—to altered tryptophan metabolism. Fecal transplants from patients raised serum aldosterone and 5-hydroxy-l-tryptophan in germ-free mice, implicating the microbiome in aldosterone excess.

papers.title: Long-term stability of the GMP-compliant recombinant BCG vaccine against human RSV under quality control analyses.
papers.summary: A GMP-manufactured lot of the recombinant BCG-based RSV vaccine (rBCG-N-RSV), which completed a phase 1 trial, met all release specifications for antigen expression, potency, safety, and efficacy over long-term quality control. In mice, vaccination enhanced virus-specific CD4+ T cell activation, anti-N IgG, respiratory function, and lung viral clearance, supporting further clinical advancement.

papers.title: Biocompatibility and antibacterial properties of ordered PLA fiber membranes fabricated via electrospinning technology.
papers.summary: Ordered electrospun poly(lactic acid) nanofiber membranes loaded with 2% moxifloxacin guided Schwann cell alignment and proliferation while nearly eradicating bacteria within two hours via membrane disruption and reactive oxygen species accumulation. With suitable mechanics and porosity, these multifunctional scaffolds integrate nerve guidance with local antibacterial protection after peripheral nerve injury.

papers.title: ARNTL2 promotes metastatic phenotypes through SERPINE1 transcription in KRAS G12D pancreatic cancer.
papers.summary: In KRAS G12D pancreatic cancer, ARNTL2 directly activates SERPINE1 transcription, driving EMT and metastasis in vitro and in vivo, with rescue experiments confirming SERPINE1 as the indispensable mediator. Clinical samples show correlated ARNTL2/SERPINE1 protein stratifying prognosis, and the axis modulates sensitivity to KRAS G12D inhibition.

papers.title: Preterm birth disrupts nephron progenitor cell dynamics predisposing to renal disease.
papers.summary: In a mouse preterm birth model, premature extrauterine life uncouples nephron progenitor proliferation from differentiation, extending the nephrogenic window without restoring nephron endowment. Preterm progenitors mount immediate unfolded protein and ER stress responses, causing permanent nephron deficit manifesting as adult glomerular hypertrophy, proteinuria, and tubular injury—highlighting the perinatal window for intervention.

papers.title: hnRNP F: An emerging orchestrator of RNA processing and gene expression.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes hnRNP F's roles in RNA metabolism—splicing, translation, mRNA stability, and telomere maintenance—and its regulation of expression. Because of high homology and functional overlap with hnRNP H/H', it integrates comparative discussion of both paralogs, providing a unified view of their biological significance in gene expression control.

papers.title: The DsbA-L paradox in protective and pathogenic stress adaptation.
papers.summary: This review frames DsbA-L/GSTK1 as a context-dependent stress-adaptability regulator: it supports adiponectin assembly, mitochondrial and organelle homeostasis, redox control, and selective autophagy, yet can sustain profibrotic or immune-metabolic programs with divergent cancer effects. The authors advocate tissue-specific modulation or downstream targeting rather than systemic activation or inhibition.

papers.title: Exercise-induced adipose tissue ADRB2-PGC1α-FGF21 signaling protects against pathological cardiac hypertrophy.
papers.summary: Three weeks of swim training activates brown and inguinal white adipose tissue via beta2-adrenoceptor-PGC1alpha signaling, inducing FGF21. Adipose-specific PGC1alpha knockout abolished exercise's protection against pressure-overload cardiac hypertrophy, and exogenous FGF21 restored it—defining an adipose-to-heart endocrine axis linking exercise to cardioprotection.

papers.title: Enhanced CRISPR-Cas3-mediated genome editing using circularized crRNAs.
papers.summary: Circularized crRNAs (crrRNAs) enhance type I-E CRISPR-Cas3 genome editing: they promote Cascade formation, mediate efficient editing at EMX1 and B2M in K562 cells with kilobase-scale deletions, show no detectable off-targets by long-read sequencing, and outperform linear crRNAs through extended intracellular stability, supporting consistent long-range deletion applications.

papers.title: Uninflamed colonic tissue harbors humoral activity linked to anti-TNF therapy non-response in ulcerative colitis.
papers.summary: Comparing ulcerative colitis patients matched at baseline but differing in anti-TNF outcome, non-responders showed higher humoral immune activity—specifically IgA plasma cell signatures—in uninflamed lamina propria, validated in an independent single-cell atlas. Epithelial and serum signatures didn't discriminate, suggesting TNF-independent humoral activity underlies primary non-response.

papers.title: Valproic acid remodels phosphatidylglycerol homeostasis and epithelial-macrophage crosstalk in inflammatory signaling.
papers.summary: Partial PGS1 loss remodels phosphatidylglycerol homeostasis and secreted phospholipid profiles in lung epithelial cells. Valproic acid similarly remodels secreted lipids while increasing anti-inflammatory POPG, and conditioned media from treated cells dampened macrophage-like inflammatory responses; VPA and POPG reduced inflammation in a quail chorioallantoic model, connecting mitochondrial PG metabolism to inflammation control.

papers.title: Linalool enables reversible immobilization for high-resolution in vivo imaging during regeneration in Schmidtea mediterranea.
papers.summary: Linalool at 2.16 mM reversibly immobilizes planarians within minutes without compromising survival or regeneration: acute or repeated daily exposures preserved blastema growth, stem cell proliferation, and brain morphology, while continuous exposure caused stress phenotypes. Defined exposure windows enable stable, high-resolution, regeneration-compatible in vivo imaging with full recovery.

papers.title: Integrating proteomics and metabolomics to reveal MAT2A for metabolic reprogramming in non-small cell lung cancer cells.
papers.summary: Integrating proteomics and metabolomics after MAT2A knockdown or AG-270 inhibition in NSCLC, the study maps MAT2A-driven rewiring of fatty acid, cholesterol, glycolytic, and transsulfuration metabolism, and nominates rational combinations: FASN inhibitor tvb-2640, LXR agonists, GLUT1 inhibitors, and PHGDH or SLC7A11 inhibitors to enhance MAT2A-targeted therapy.

papers.title: Characterizing cellular receptor dynamics in live fluorescence imaging using stochastic modeling and machine learning.
papers.summary: An interpretable machine-learning framework combining trajectory geometry with random forest classification distinguishes five receptor motion classes in single-particle tracking data. Applied to the HIV co-receptor CCR5, it shows agonist psc-RANTES shifts dynamics from intermittent diffusion toward confined, attraction-driven motion—linking stochastic models to receptor clustering and internalization states.

papers.title: Trop-1/EpCAM Thr115 is a driver of hyperproliferative cell repair and of severe lung damage in COVID-19.
papers.summary: The Trop-1/EpCAM T115 variant drives hyperproliferative repair: T115 but not M115 induces cell growth in human and mouse cells, and COVID-19 patients carrying T115 mount aberrant alveolar hyperproliferation with hyaline membranes, computed to reduce oxygen diffusion up to 100-fold. T115 EpCAM emerges as a driver of severe COVID-19 lung damage and a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Generation of T cell containing adipose tissue organoids.
papers.summary: Researchers generated adipose tissue organoids containing infiltrated T cells, with distinct ratios of regulatory versus CD4+ effector T cells across conditions, and LPS-driven inflammatory mimicry enhanced CD4+ infiltration. The model provides an ex vivo, near-physiological platform for studying adipose-resident T cells across fat depots beyond mouse and donor samples.

papers.title: Development of a lethal adult mouse model of Coxsackievirus B1 infection for antiviral research.
papers.summary: Using reverse genetics on a clinical isolate, researchers established a lethal Coxsackievirus B1 model in immunocompetent adult BALB/c mice, with viral tropism for pancreas, liver, and skeletal muscle causing extensive inflammation. Passive immunization dose-dependently reduced replication, damage, weight loss, and mortality, providing a platform for antiviral and vaccine development.

papers.title: Amphiregulin shapes mitochondrial delivery and immune modulation by microvescicles.
papers.summary: LPS stimulation of amniotic epithelial cells remodels microvesicle cargo, enriching 101 metabolic and regulatory proteins including amphiregulin. AREG silencing reduced microvesicle uptake by PBMCs and T cells and diminished their suppression of proliferation and NFAT activation, identifying inflammation-driven AREG as key to immunomodulatory cell-free therapy potential.

papers.title: KMT5A maintains muscle stem cell quiescence through epigenetic regulation of Notch signaling.
papers.summary: The H4K20 monomethyltransferase KMT5A sustains muscle stem cell quiescence by depositing H4K20me1 at Notch loci, maintaining transcriptional competence of canonical Notch genes including Rbpj. Genetic Notch restoration rescued quiescence but not post-activation survival or regenerative output, distinguishing homeostatic KMT5A loss from physiological activation mechanisms.

papers.title: Levocarnitine attenuates diabetic seminal vesicle fibrosis in association with improved lipid metabolism and reduced ER stress.
papers.summary: In diabetic mice, seminal vesicles show atrophy, fibrosis, altered lipid profiles, reduced PPARalpha/PGC-1alpha, and increased IRE1 ER stress and apoptosis. Levocarnitine attenuated these changes in vivo and profibrotic responses in vitro, with PPARalpha overexpression reproducing protection, supporting further evaluation for diabetes-associated reproductive tract injury.

papers.title: Zebrafish larvae reveal early neuropathology and host responses to nervous necrosis virus.
papers.summary: Bath-immersion infection of 4-day-post-fertilization zebrafish larvae with nervous necrosis virus produced progressive viral accumulation, retinal disruption, mitochondrial swelling, virus-like particles in brain, and altered locomotion. Transcriptomics revealed antiviral, oxidative stress, and cytokine pathways activated alongside suppressed neuronal maintenance, DNA replication, and cell cycle genes—an early host-response profile.

papers.title: Proteomic analyses of seasonal human respiratory viruses unravel changes related to antiviral, inflammatory, and cell death pathways.
papers.summary: Label-free quantitative proteomics of A549 lung cells infected with seasonal coronaviruses, influenza A, or RSV showed dysregulation of lipid metabolism, transport, cell death, and inflammatory proteins, with RSV inducing the most profound response. Enzymes, ion channels, kinases, transcription regulators, and receptors were most affected, suggesting therapeutic intervention targets.

papers.title: Chronic chikungunya is associated with decreased anti-CHIKV antibody titers, neutralizing capacity, and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.
papers.summary: In chikungunya patients, anti-CHIKV IgG and IgM titers declined between 3 and 6 months, with lower 6-month titers associated with chronic disease. Chronic patients showed reduced antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity but preserved phagocytosis and complement deposition; females had higher E2 antibodies and phagocytosis, detailing Fc effector contributions to disease outcome.

papers.title: A cetacean-specific CNE suppresses osteogenesis to drive appendicular modification in secondary aquatic adaptation.
papers.summary: A cetacean-specific conserved non-coding element, CNE300, shows accelerated evolution and reduced regulatory activity. Knock-in mice carrying the cetacean element developed shortened limb bones and altered trabecular architecture with reduced osteogenesis and a cartilage-biased transcriptional program, directly demonstrating a regulatory mechanism underlying cetacean appendicular remodeling for aquatic life.

papers.title: Transcriptomic landscape of microglia in mouse models of social dysfunction and oxytocin-mediated recovery.
papers.summary: Embryonic valproic acid exposure induces transcriptional abnormalities and altered spatial distribution of paraventricular hypothalamus microglia in mice. Neonatal oxytocin neuron activation reversed a subset of these changes, and microglial manipulation normalized oxytocin gene expression, supporting bidirectional neuron-microglia interactions underlying social dysfunction in neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.title: SingleCellMQC: A comprehensive quality control workflow for single-cell multi-omics.
papers.summary: SingleCellMQC is an open-source R package providing unified, modality-aware quality control for single-cell RNA, antibody-derived tag, and immune repertoire data. It implements multi-level QC with empirical thresholds, tissue-specific references, and outlier detection, generating interactive HTML reports, and was validated on datasets up to over one million cells.

papers.title: CoexpressDeconvolve enables reference-free single-cell-resolution deconvolution from spot-based spatial transcriptomics.
papers.summary: CoexpressDeconvolve is a reference-free spatial transcriptomics deconvolution framework combining housekeeping-library-size calibration with topic modeling to recover integer cell counts and cell-type-specific transcriptomes per spot. Benchmarked against Tangram, cell2location, and STdeconvolve, it achieved the lowest cell-count error and highest per-slide concordance, resolving tumor microenvironments in breast and tongue squamous carcinoma.

papers.title: Single nucleus transcriptomics reveals ITGA8-driven fibroblast remodeling in rheumatic valvular atrial fibrillation.
papers.summary: Single-nucleus RNA-seq of left atrial tissue from rheumatic valvular atrial fibrillation patients identified an expanded ITGA8-enriched fibroblast state associated with matrix remodeling. Functional assays showed ITGA8 promotes fibroblast proliferation, migration, and matrix production, and fibroblast-targeted ITGA8 suppression reduced atrial fibrosis and AF susceptibility in a rat model.

papers.title: Hippuric acid contributes to NK-cell activation with dependence on TLR2 in chronic hepatitis B complicated by MASLD.
papers.summary: Chronic hepatitis B patients with MASLD show increased NK cell frequency and activation, with TLR2 upregulation correlating with metabolic parameters and liver stiffness. Plasma metabolomics identified hippuric acid enriched in these patients, promoting NK activation partially via TLR2, and hippuric acid-stimulated NK cells activated stellate-like LX-2 cells, linking metabolism to hepatic immunopathology.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omic profiling of heterogeneous PROCR(+) cells in mouse mammary gland and its implication for breast cancer.
papers.summary: Integrating enrichment with single-cell transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility across mammary gland development, this study resolves heterogeneous PROCR+ subpopulations including a CDH5-negative, COL1A1-positive mammary stem cell state with high potency and EMT-associated programs. Analogous human populations exist, with the stem signature enriched in triple-negative and claudin-low tumors.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals that tenocyte-derived MIF contributes to tendon injury pathogenesis.
papers.summary: Reanalyzing tendon injury single-cell data reveals mesenchymal-immune signaling dominated by MIF via CD74/CXCR4 and ACKR3 between tenocytes and myeloid cells during acute injury. MIF expression rose in injured tendon with inflammatory and apoptotic changes, and hydrogel-delivered MIF inhibitor 4-IPP (F127@4-IPP) reduced inflammation and improved histological outcomes in mice.

papers.title: Metabolic reprogramming-mediated therapeutic resistance in renal cell carcinoma: Mechanisms and targeted intervention strategies.
papers.summary: This review examines how renal cell carcinoma reprograms glucose, lipid, and amino acid metabolism to drive resistance against targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and radiotherapy. It proposes strategies including metabolism-targeting drugs, nanoparticle co-delivery, combination regimens, and personalized approaches to overcome metabolic resistance mechanisms in metastatic disease.

papers.title: FoxO transcription factors coordinate the urea cycle and gluconeogenesis by controlling Ass1.
papers.summary: FoxO transcription factors directly regulate hepatic argininosuccinate synthase 1 (Ass1) via a fasting-inducible enhancer element. FoxO1/3a knockdown reduced Ass1, lowered blood glucose, and altered urea-cycle amino acids independent of KLF15; Ass1 silencing impaired glucose production from pyruvate and lactate while overexpression rescued it, coupling ureagenesis to gluconeogenesis during fasting.

papers.title: Investigation of plasma-derived extracellular vesicles in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients.
papers.summary: Plasma extracellular vesicles from hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients show altered cellular origin—enriched platelet-derived CD41a+ vesicles with reduced neutrophil and lymphatic endothelial sources—and proteomic signatures of platelet activation and thrombo-inflammation. Multivariable EV protein models discriminated patients from controls comparably to plasma, complementing biomarker discovery.

papers.title: MORC1 coordinates TRIM28 interaction and nuclear condensate formation for transposon silencing.
papers.summary: MORC1 forms nuclear condensates via an intrinsically disordered region with a bipartite nuclear localization signal and concentrates the TRIM28-SETDB1 corepressor within them. An IDR-deficient mutant retains TRIM28 binding but fails to condense and occupies heterochromatin-embedded transposons more strongly, supporting a model where restrained IDR-dependent condensate formation shapes silencing function.

papers.title: RAD51AP1-MYC-Sam68 positive transcriptional feedback loop maintains lung cancer stemness.
papers.summary: RAD51AP1 promotes lung cancer stemness by transcriptionally upregulating MYC, MYC induces SAM68, and SAM68 enhances RAD51AP1 transcription—forming a positive feedback loop. Confirmed via CUT&Tag, reporter, and chromatin assays in vitro and in vivo, this cascade offers a targetable node for reversing stemness in lung cancer.

papers.title: IRX1 suppresses cervical squamous cell carcinoma progression by downregulating ACLY expression to inhibit lipid synthesis.
papers.summary: IRX1, downregulated by promoter hypermethylation in cervical cancer, recruits NME3 to the ACLY promoter forming a repressive complex that curbs de novo fatty acid synthesis—reducing acetyl-CoA, malonyl-CoA, triglycerides, cholesterol, and lipid droplets. ACLY overexpression partially reversed tumor suppression, establishing IRX1 as a metabolic tumor suppressor.

papers.title: Single-cell mapping of homocysteine-induced perturbations in avian embryogenesis using LMO and BD rhapsody transcriptomics.
papers.summary: Combining lipid-modified oligonucleotide cell tagging with BD Rhapsody in chick embryos enables multiplexed single-cell transcriptomics across homocysteine conditions without species-specific reagents. Non-integrated analysis preserved cluster-specific signatures that integration masked, revealing homocysteine-associated changes in neuromesodermal progenitors linked to posterior mesodermal and axis elongation defects.

papers.title: Bottlenecked reproduction enables cooperating bacteria to purge cheaters.
papers.summary: This hypothesis proposes that reproduction at cooperative colonization foci is bottlenecked—extremely few cells initiate dispersal—allowing bacterial populations to purge cheaters carrying loss-of-function mutations in sociality genes. Escaping cheaters fail at subsequent reproduction at new sites, and interrogating this mechanism may reveal vulnerabilities exploitable against bacterial diseases.

papers.title: Early life high-fat diet exposure modulates adult metabolic phenotypes in Drosophila.
papers.summary: Larval high-fat diet exposure in Drosophila durably remodels adult fat body transcriptomes—repressing TCA and oxidative phosphorylation genes, raising reactive oxygen species, and impairing mitochondrial bioenergetics—while reshaping gut microbiota. Adult nicotinamide riboside, alpha-ketoglutarate, or commensal bacteria partially restored redox balance, respiration, and lifespan, suggesting reversible metabolic programming.

papers.title: TRPV4-driven ATP release activates CFTR through ADORA2B and P2RY2 receptors in the airway epithelium.
papers.summary: TRPV4 activation in airway epithelium triggers ATP release that activates CFTR through P2Y2 purinergic and A2B adenosine receptors, nearly abolished by receptor blockade. Because TRPV4 and CFTR occupy distinct cell types, this paracrine purinergic axis links mechanical and chemical stimuli to airway surface hydration and mucociliary clearance.

papers.title: A streamlined protocol for small-scale protoplast generation and CRISPR/Cpf1-mediated genome editing in Fusarium oxysporum.
papers.summary: An integrated CRISPR/Cpf1 platform for Fusarium oxysporum combines filter-column small-scale protoplast generation reducing enzyme use, shorter guide RNA design with staggered cleavage, and minimal homology arms reducing cloning complexity. Validated by gene targeting and pathogenicity assays, it provides affordable, high-throughput editing for fungal research and agricultural biotechnology.

papers.title: Stroma-oriented tumor microenvironment facilitates intraosseous ameloblastoma tumor growth.
papers.summary: In an orthotopic intraosseous ameloblastoma model, ameloblastoma-derived mesenchymal stromal cells and their extracellular vesicle-enriched secretome enhanced epithelial cell stemness, EMT, and tumorigenicity via a microRNA signature. Single-nucleus ATAC-RNA-seq confirmed dynamic EMT states, establishing a stromal-oriented platform for tumor-stroma crosstalk and therapeutic target discovery.

papers.title: Differential activation of TCA cycle activity and PDH flux by dichloroacetate in skeletal muscle measured by hyperpolarized [2-(13)C,3-(2)H(3)]pyruvate.
papers.summary: Hyperpolarized [2-13C,3-2H3]pyruvate magnetic resonance tracks label incorporation into TCA cycle-derived glutamate in rat skeletal muscle. Dichloroacetate raised [1-13C]acetyl-L-carnitine more than [5-13C]glutamate, showing disproportionate PDH versus TCA flux increases—demonstrating these fluxes aren't tightly coupled and validating a robust in vivo mitochondrial metabolism probe.

papers.title: Anti-inflammatory and phosphorylation effects of CFTR modulator triple therapy in cystic fibrosis.
papers.summary: In children under 12 with cystic fibrosis, three months of elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor therapy produced anti-inflammatory effects, epigenetic modulation, and increased protein kinase activity on blood RNA-seq, proteomics, and phosphoproteomics—partially reversing baseline systemic inflammation, transporter deficiency, and reduced kinase and GTPase activity, with biomarker potential for treatment monitoring.

papers.title: PIWIL4 regulates gene expression and piRNA levels in RSV-infected airway epithelial cells.
papers.summary: PIWIL4 is expressed in airway epithelial cells during RSV infection, and its knockdown—without affecting viral replication—reduced cytokine and growth factor secretion, altered gene and piRNA expression, and modulated cytokine, metabolic, and airway remodeling pathways. Limited piRNA-target overlap suggests PIWIL4 acts partly independently of piRNAs in antiviral responses.

papers.title: Exercise-associated epigenetic remodeling and TCR repertoire dynamics in Lynch syndrome carriers.
papers.summary: A 52-week aerobic cycling intervention in Lynch syndrome carriers produced compartment-specific DNA methylation changes—including innate immune activation in cell-free DNA and oncogenic pathway repression in tissue—repressed ISL1, altered FLCN methylation, and increased T cell receptor repertoire diversity with tissue-specific clonal convergence, suggesting antigen-driven immune remodeling as exercise's protective mechanism.

papers.title: FASN-mediated de novo lipogenesis promotes ceramide accumulation and myocardial damage in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: In arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, desmosomal dysfunction drives plakoglobin nuclear translocation, cooperating with SREBP1 to activate fatty acid synthase transcription. Resultant de novo lipogenesis generates lipotoxic ceramides causing cardiomyocyte apoptosis; isotope tracing, lipidomics, and RNA-seq support this, and FASN inhibition with orlistat reduced lipid accumulation and improved cardiac function and survival.

papers.title: Community: Component based differential cell communication analysis in large multi-sample case-control scRNAseq datasets.
papers.summary: Community is an R package for differential cell-cell communication analysis in multi-sample case-control scRNA-seq, decomposing changes into cell type abundance, active signaling fraction, and expression components. Applied to ulcerative colitis, melanoma immunotherapy, and AML, it captured disease- and response-associated communication shifts with improved robustness and scalability over existing tools.

papers.title: The Sox2 regulatory region 42 produces enhancer RNAs that influence neuronal migration during cortical development.
papers.summary: SOX2 regulatory region 42, 42 kb downstream of SOX2, shows open chromatin, active histone marks, and bidirectional enhancer RNA transcription in neural progenitors. CRISPR deletion altered progenitor dynamics, neuronal migration, and cortical lamination without changing SOX2 expression, and in vivo enhancer RNA knockdown impaired migration—identifying functional enhancer transcription in cortical development.

papers.title: Identification of elements determining KIR gene demethylation at the CD56-bright stage of NK cell development.
papers.summary: During NK cell development, KIR gene demethylation occurs at the CD56-bright stage with 5-hydroxymethylcytosine deposition at a CREB site adjacent to the Runx-binding promoter site, driven by Runx-recruited TET proteins. Demethylation is delayed relative to other lineage genes, indicating a high threshold and a defined window for KIR activation in developing NK cells.

papers.title: Synergistic disruption of redox and energy homeostasis via high-entropy layered double hydroxide nanozymes for enhanced tumor therapy.
papers.summary: High-entropy layered double hydroxide nanozymes anchored with platinum clusters combine glucose oxidase-like activity—depleting intratumoral glucose—with redox disruption, overcoming tumor energy-mediated oxidative stress resistance. These PT-LDH nanozymes inhibited tumor growth in vitro and in vivo with minimal toxicity, demonstrating high-entropy engineering as a practical nanozyme design strategy.

papers.title: MAPK-driven MYC/p21 axis controls senescence bypass and BCL-XL dependence in vincristine-resistant rhabdomyosarcoma.
papers.summary: Vincristine-resistant fusion-negative rhabdomyosarcoma is driven by enhanced MAPK signaling and MYC-mediated repression of p21 that bypasses senescence, validated in post-chemotherapy patient specimens. Resistant cells show BCL-XL dependence, and combined MEK plus BCL-XL inhibition eradicated resistant tumors in vitro and in vivo, offering a preclinical rationale for refractory disease.

papers.title: Tetrazine-based bioorthogonal reactions to image hypoxia in cancer cells.
papers.summary: Trans-cyclooctene-clickable 2-nitroimidazoles combined with tetrazine-functionalized probes enable bioorthogonal inverse-electron-demand Diels-Alder imaging of tumor hypoxia in 2D, 3D spheroids, and patient-derived organoids. A click-to-release approach quantified released probe diffusion and bystander effects, opening a route to in vivo hypoxia visualization relevant to cancer therapy resistance.

papers.title: The CNNM-binding interface drives PRL-3-dependent tumor progression in de novo cancer models.
papers.summary: Using structure-guided separation-of-function PRL-3 mutants in de novo zebrafish rhabdomyosarcoma and T-ALL models plus human cancer cells, the CNNM-binding interface—not phosphatase activity—drove magnesium retention, stress tolerance, tumor growth, and leukemia progression. Catalytic inhibition alone may thus inadequately suppress PRL-3-driven malignancy.

papers.title: Importin-8 silencing reduces Ataxin-3 aggregation and alleviates Machado-Joseph disease/spinocerebellar ataxia type 3.
papers.summary: Importin-8 (IPO8) mRNA is elevated in Machado-Joseph disease, and IPO8 silencing reduced ataxin-3 aggregation and neuronal dysfunction in vitro and in vivo while alleviating ataxic traits. Potential mechanisms involve modulation of NF-kB/p65 and Argonaute-2 pathways, nominating IPO8 as a therapeutic target for this polyglutamine ataxia.

papers.title: TNFα-dependent modulation of WT1-MMP9 regulatory axis links developmental and inflammatory pathways in glaucoma.
papers.summary: Targeted sequencing of 586 primary congenital glaucoma cases identified rare WT1 nuclear export sequence variants. WT1 represses MMP9 in trabecular meshwork cells, but TNF-alpha triggers nitric oxide-dependent WT1 nuclear export, relieving repression; export or nitric oxide synthase inhibition reversed this, linking developmental and inflammatory mechanisms in glaucoma.

papers.title: Hierarchical modeling of tumor subtypes in cell lines using large-scale genomic datasets.
papers.summary: A hierarchical classification framework aligns 802 cancer cell lines with 5,612 TCGA tumors and 8,939 normal tissues, separating oncogenic from tissue-of-origin signals to improve subtype annotation. Achieving 89% cross-validation and 75-80% external balanced accuracy, it reassigned 43 cell lines and identified clinically relevant underrepresented tumor subtypes for translational research.

papers.title: Transcriptional landscape of direct reprogramming toward the hematopoietic lineage.
papers.summary: A single-cell transcriptomic reference atlas of hematopoietic reprogramming benchmarks direct fibroblast-to-HSC conversion. Long-read single-cell RNA-seq of CD34+ reprogrammed cells showed progressive fibroblast identity loss with early hematopoietic and endothelial induction, placing cells in an intermediate state, with isoform-level remodeling revealing regulation gene-level analyses miss.

papers.title: NF-κB-driven immune checkpoint knockdown and cytokine expression in cancer cells for tumor immunotherapy.
papers.summary: An NF-kappaB-activated gene cassette produces IL-15 and microRNAs silencing PD-L1 and CD47 selectively in cancer cells, where high NF-kappaB activity drives expression while low basal activity keeps it silent in normal cells. AAV2 delivery showed significant antitumor effects, tumor selectivity, and biosafety across murine solid tumor models.

papers.title: Phospholipase D2 acts upstream of PI4P 5-kinases in the response of neurons to extracellular viscosity.
papers.summary: Developing neurons respond to extracellular viscosity through a pathway requiring membrane glycolipids and phospholipase D2, which acts upstream of PI4P 5-kinases to generate PI(4,5)P2 as an inhibitory signal restricting axon extension. High viscosity increases glucosylceramide GM1 in neurites, negatively regulating PLD2 and linking physical environment to axon growth decisions.

papers.title: Extracellular vesicles for liquid biopsy in major depressive disorder: Human evidence and clinical translation.
papers.summary: This narrative review appraises extracellular vesicle biomarkers for major depressive disorder, noting how pre-analytical variability, inconsistent isolation, and uncertain brain-enrichment specificity limit replication. It argues EV profiling should complement clinical phenotyping, neuroimaging, and digital measures in precision psychiatry rather than serve standalone, and outlines standardization and validation roadmaps.

papers.title: Extracellular matrix composition and stiffness regulates progesterone responsiveness and decidualization.
papers.summary: Using hydrogels mimicking physiological stiffness, ECM ligands differentially regulate decidualization: laminin slows secretory responses while stabilizing FOXO1 and WNT4, fibronectin produces quicker but less stable differentiation, and stiff matrices override these cues to inhibit progesterone responses. Endometriotic lesions mirror this, with stiffer sites showing more fibronectin and less decidualization.

papers.title: Reducing sialylation in melanoma increases classical pathway-mediated complement activation.
papers.summary: Metabolic or enzymatic reduction of sialylation in melanoma increases classical pathway complement activation—enhancing C3 deposition and membrane attack complex formation—mediated by increased immunoglobulin binding to tumor cells. This positions complement as a relevant soluble anti-tumor mechanism when sialylation is targeted, complementing cellular immune responses.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics of Ciona adult brains reveals functional zonalization and insights into neural gland function.
papers.summary: Spatial transcriptomics of the adult Ciona neural complex with computational super-resolution resolved tissue domains and molecular zonalization within the cerebral ganglion's cortex and medulla. The neural gland shows extracellular matrix and cell-cell interaction gene enrichment, suggesting a homeostatic signaling interface reminiscent of primitive meninges or choroid plexus.

papers.title: Dynamic interactions with neuroblasts promote oligodendrocyte progenitor migration to injured cortex.
papers.summary: In neonatal cortical injury, ventricular-subventricular zone-derived oligodendrocyte progenitor cells migrate to lesions alongside neuroblasts via dynamic heterotypic contacts. Live imaging and 3D culture show neuroblast contact enhances OPC motility through transient adherens junctions that form and dissolve during migration, revealing cooperative progenitor navigation supporting remyelination.
